comparison: Both evaluations support the finding that single-nucleus (SN) sequencing captures STB better than single-cell (SC) methods. OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative validation (8:1 ratio matching expected 9:1 from stereological studies), while peer reviewers highlight the necessity of using both techniques and the added rationale for SN over SC. Both mark as SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Both evaluations support the identification and characterization of three STB subtypes (C44-C47, C72-C74). OpenEval notes that C72-C74 are Discussion interpretations and that the terminal differentiation hypothesis (C74) lacks direct validation. Peer reviewers confirm the authors removed definitive language about STB-3 terminal status and now present alternative hypotheses, which both evaluations accept as appropriate. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations strongly support the findings about culture condition effects on STB subtype proportions (C41-C47, C64-C66). OpenEval notes internal consistency and multiple validation methods (RNA-FISH) but mentions that specific p-values are not always provided. Peer reviewers emphasize the improvements in the STBout model and the importance of TO orientation. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the identification of RYBP as a key regulator (C49-C51). OpenEval includes C78 (knockout validation showing STB-2 marker upregulation) and notes incomplete mechanistic understanding. Peer reviewers accept the identification and localization but do not explicitly reference C78 in their evaluation. Both mark as SUPPORTED with convergence of computational and experimental validation.

Both evaluations support the RYBP/AFF1 knockout findings (C9-C11, C52-C54). OpenEval includes C78 and notes that bulk RNA-seq cannot definitively determine cell-autonomous effects. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as the first CRISPR application in TO models and accept the conclusions about regulatory function. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the pseudotime trajectory analysis (C48). OpenEval notes the trajectory is consistent with known biology but acknowledges that pseudotime infers temporal ordering from snapshot data without lineage tracing. Peer reviewers accept the trajectory analysis as valid and note the authors clarified their interpretation by removing definitive claims about terminal states. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the comparative analysis between organoids and tissue (C55-C63). OpenEval emphasizes hormone expression patterns matching gestational changes and notes organoids resemble first trimester tissue as a stated limitation. Peer reviewers accept the comparative findings and note the study identifies both conserved and distinct profiles. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C57-C58 regarding CTB conservation versus STB diversity. OpenEval groups these with broader tissue-organoid comparisons (C55-C63), while peer reviewers evaluate C57-C58 separately as part of functional characterization. Both evaluations support these findings and mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations support the TSC versus TO comparison (C67-C69). OpenEval notes distinct transcriptional profiles despite similar proportions and mentions the analysis is limited to one TSC dataset. Peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive model characterization without challenge. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Both evaluations address speculative/hypothesis claims (C75-C77, C81). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting these are Discussion hypotheses about environmental mechanisms (oxygen, tension, flow) that are not directly tested. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable hypotheses and interpretations for future work. This represents a difference in evaluation stringency for speculative claims.

Partial overlap on C70-C71 regarding mitotic proportions and lineage specification mechanisms. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED but notes these are Discussion interpretations requiring lineage tracing validation. Peer reviewers group these with other hypotheses (C75-C77, C80-C81) and mark as SUPPORTED, accepting them as appropriate speculation. Both accept the claims but OpenEval is more cautious about mechanistic interpretations.

Both evaluations support C79 (mouse RYBP data citation). OpenEval notes species differences limit extrapolation and treats it as a discussion point. Peer reviewers accept it as contextual citation supporting RYBP relevance. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C80 regarding extrinsic regulation of hormone expression. OpenEval groups C79-C80 together as reasonable inferences and marks as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers group C80 with broader hypotheses (C70-C71, C75-C77, C81) and mark as SUPPORTED. Both accept the interpretation.

Minor overlap on C66 (EVTenrich model validation). OpenEval groups C66 with culture condition effects on lineage specification. Peer reviewers evaluate EVTenrich characterization separately, accepting it as part of comprehensive model validation. Both mark as SUPPORTED.

Peer reviewers evaluated background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C12-C33) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide appropriate context with citations. OpenEval did not produce a separate evaluation for these background claims, likely focusing on primary findings rather than contextual information.

Peer reviewers evaluated methodological claims (C82-C85) as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting methods as appropriate. OpenEval did not produce a separate evaluation for these methodological details, as they appear to focus on scientific findings rather than technical procedures.
